arxiv-2110-06414.creator: Yuqian Wei, Bin Chen (陈彬), Sijie Yu (余思捷), Haimin Wang, Ju Jing, Dale E. Gary
arxiv-2110-06414.description: Abstract Magnetic flux ropes are the centerpiece of solar eruptions. Direct measurements for the magnetic field of flux ropes are crucial for understanding the triggering and energy release processes, yet they remain heretofore elusive. arxiv-2202-05307.title: Sub-cycle time-resolved nondipole dynamics in tunneling ionization
arxiv-2202-05307.creator: Michael Klaiber, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, Christoph H. Keitel
arxiv-2202-05307.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Michael Klaiber, Karen Z. Hatsagortsyan, Christoph H. Keitel. The electron nondipole dynamics in tunneling ionization in an elliptically polarized laser field is investigated theoretically using a relativistic Coulomb-corrected strong field approximation (SFA) based on the eikonal approximation of the Klein-Gordon equation. We calculate attoclock angle-resolved light-front momentum distributions at different ellipticities of the laser field in quasistatic and nonadiabatic regimes and analyze them with an improved Simpleman model. The nondipole correlations between longitudinal and transverse momentum components are examined.

arxiv-2209-06042.title: Generalised Automatic Anatomy Finder (GAAF): A general framework for 3D location-finding in CT scans
arxiv-2209-06042.creator: Edward G. A. Henderson, Eliana M. Vasquez Osorio, Marcel van Herk, Andrew F. Green
arxiv-2209-06042.description: Abstract We present GAAF, a G eneralised A utomatic A natomy F inder, for the identification of generic anatomical locations in 3D CT scans. GAAF is an end-to-end pipeline, with dedicated modules for data pre-processing, model training, and inference. At it’s core, GAAF uses a custom a localisation convolutional neural network (CNN).

arxiv-2211-15971.title: Democratizing Machine Learning for Interdisciplinary Scholars: Report on Organizing the NLP+CSS Online Tutorial Series Conference: ; ; CCS: Computing methodologies Artificial intelligence CCS: Social and professional topics Computing education programs
arxiv-2211-15971.creator: Ian Stewart, Katherine A. Keith
arxiv-2211-15971.description: Abstract . Many scientific fields---including biology, health, education, and the social sciences---use machine learning (ML) to help them analyze data at an unprecedented scale. However, ML researchers who develop advanced methods rarely provide detailed tutorials showing how to apply these methods. Existing tutorials are often costly to participants, presume extensive programming knowledge, and are not tailored to specific application fields.

arxiv-2410-02147.title: Efficient Source-Free Time-Series Adaptation via Parameter Subspace Disentanglement
arxiv-2410-02147.creator: Gaurav Patel †, Chris Sandino ‡, Behrooz Mahasseni ‡, Ellen Zippi ‡
arxiv-2410-02147.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a framework for efficient Source-Free Domain Adaptation (SFDA) in the context of time-series, focusing on enhancing both parameter efficiency and data-sample utilization. Our approach introduces an improved paradigm for source-model preparation and target-side adaptation, aiming to enhance training efficiency during target adaptation.

arxiv-2501-09750.title: Coming full circle
arxiv-2501-09750.creator: Markus Frembs Institut für Theoretische Physik, Leibniz Universität Hannover, Appelstraße 2, 30167 Hannover, Germany Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University, Onna, Okinawa 904 0495, Japan Centre for Quantum Dynamics, Griffith University, Yugambeh Country, Gold Coast, QLD 4222
arxiv-2501-09750.description: Abstract Contextuality is a key distinguishing feature between classical and quantum physics. It expresses a fundamental obstruction to describing quantum theory using classical concepts. In turn, when understood as a resource for quantum computation, it is expected to hold the key to quantum advantage.

arxiv-2507-03831.title: Query-Based Adaptive Aggregation for Multi-Dataset Joint Training Toward Universal Visual Place Recognition
arxiv-2507-03831.creator: Jiuhong Xiao, Yang Zhou, Giuseppe Loianno
arxiv-2507-03831.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jiuhong Xiao, Yang Zhou, Giuseppe Loianno. Deep learning methods for Visual Place Recognition (VPR) have advanced significantly, largely driven by large-scale datasets. However, most existing approaches are trained on a single dataset, which can introduce dataset-specific inductive biases and limit model generalization. While multi-dataset joint training offers a promising solution for developing universal VPR models, divergences among training datasets can saturate limited information capacity in feature aggregation layers, leading to suboptimal performance.

pmc-11610548.title: Conversion therapy with chemoimmunotherapy induced pCR in a stage IV lung squamous cell carcinoma patient harboring EGFR exon 20 insertion
pmc-11610548.creator: Mingjin Xu, Xingfa Huo, Chuantao Zhang, Xuchen Zhang, Huiyun Wang, Hongmin Yang, Nan Ge, Yongjie Wang, Helei Hou
pmc-11610548.description: This case study details an innovative conversion therapy strategy in a 58-year-old Asian male with baseline stage cT4N1M1b advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) harboring a rare EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation with concurrent high PD-L1 expression who achieved a pathologic complete response (pCR) after preoperative immunotherapy plus chemotherapy.

pmc-13528346.title: Oral care interventions in adult intensive care unit patients: A systematic review of oral and respiratory outcomes
pmc-13528346.creator: Vincenzo Ronsivalle, Paola Lo Giudice, Francesco Leonforte, Simona Santonocito, Giulia Tropea, Marco Cicciù
pmc-13528346.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAdult intensive care unit (ICU) patients, especially those receiving mechanical ventilation, are prone to rapid oral and mucosal deterioration, which may contribute to respiratory infection. Oral care protocols vary widely and their effects on clinically important outcomes remain uncertain.ObjectivesTo synthesize evidence regarding oral care interventions in adult intensive care patients across oral, microbiological, respiratory, and major clinical outcomes, including feasibility and safety when reported.MethodsPubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and LILACS were searched from inception to February 1, 2025.

pmc-13541853.title: Effects of tyrosine kinase inhibitors on skeletal muscle metabolism: a link with muscle complaints
pmc-13541853.creator: Lando Janssen, Charlotte A. Hoogstraten, Neeltje A. E. Allard, Tom J. J. Schirris, Maria T. E. Hopman, Nicole M. A. Blijlevens, Silvie Timmers
pmc-13541853.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients receiving tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) often report muscle complaints (MC). Strategies to prevent or attenuate these muscle complaints remain enigmatic as the underlying mechanism is unclear, although a central role for mitochondria is proposed. We investigated the effects of TKIs on cellular metabolism in muscle biopsies of CML patients (n = 20), compared with healthy controls (n = 10) and whether these changes may be linked to muscle complaints.
